texts.li: [theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} and the others from {PLACE} came up the road slowly, the way people walk who have been in bed a long time, now that {TALE} has run its course there. They have brought a gift from {FACTION}, worth about {COUNT} silver, for the medicine the colony sent.\n\nThey'd also like to say the names of their dead aloud, away from the houses where they died.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} puts the gift in {A_nameDef}'s hands and says the names of three children who are alive because of the colony. Then {X_nameDef} and the others turn for home.
{X_nameDef} is told to take the gift back to {PLACE}, where the living need it more. {X_nameDef} looks at {A_nameDef} a long moment, nods, and ties the bundle shut again.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has carried the first good harvest since {TALE} up from {PLACE}, {COUNT} measures of {THING} in sacks on the bearers' backs. The colony fed them in the hungry months, and {FACTION} do not forget a thing like that.

lines.li: The {THING} goes into the stores. {X_nameDef} won't stay for a meal, and says the fields at home won't plant themselves.
The long table is set and {X_nameDef} is put at the head of it, between the colony's oldest and youngest. {X_nameDef} is asked about the fields at {PLACE} until the plates are empty.
{X_nameDef} hears where the grain should go instead, and smiles. "We'll tell them who sent it," {X_nameDef} says, and picks up the sacks again.
{X_nameDef} puts both hands on the cold green metal as if it might be warm. {FACTION} take it home between them, and promise it will ring for the colony too.
{FACTION} pay the bronze's worth in full and haul it away. They are polite about it. They are also counting.
{A_nameDef} and two others set off down the river with it, slung on poles, and the people from {PLACE} singing in front. {FACTION} will feed them well at the other end.

texts.li: [flag:sheltered] The two travelers who waited out {TALE} by the colony's fire are back, as they promised. Mud to the knee, grinning, with {COUNT} measures of {THING} for planting from {PLACE}'s best fields.\n\n{X_nameDef} says the debt isn't paid until the seed is in the ground.

[helped] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come up from {PLACE} now the roads are open. They'd have frozen, {X_nameDef} says, without the colony's wood in {TALE}. The thanks come as {COUNT} measures of {THING} for the planting.

lines.li: The seed goes into the stores, and the visitors sit down to a hot meal from the colony's kitchen. They talk about the winter as if it were years ago.
The visitors and the colony go out to the fields with the seed between them, and the first rows of it go into the wet spring ground.
{A_nameDef} hands the seed back and says the winter's debt was paid by the company. They argue, and lose, and go home with it.
The {THING} goes into the stores, and {X_nameDef} goes back down the road before anyone can try to pay for it.
{X_nameDef} is sat at the head of the table, and the colony eats with an old friend for an evening. It's a plain supper, and {X_nameDef} says it's the best {X_pronoun} has had all year.
{X_nameDef} is sent home with the seed still on {X_possessive} back, for {PLACE}'s own hungry. {X_nameDef} says {FACTION} will be ashamed of themselves and proud of the colony, both at once.

texts.li: [ignored] An elder of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come up from {PLACE} on foot. During {TALE} the colony sent nothing, and {X_nameDef} has come to say so, face to face, and to see what the colony says back.\n\n{X_nameDef} has a list of names, and hasn't started reading it yet.

lines.li: The silver is carried out to {X_nameDef} for {PLACE}'s widows, and {A_nameDef} says plainly that the colony should have helped. {X_nameDef} doesn't thank anyone, and doesn't need to.
{X_nameDef} reads the names to the colony, and {A_nameDef} answers when the list is done: the colony was wrong. Some of the colony can't look at {X_nameDef} while it's said.
{A_nameDef} says the colony's first duty was to its own. {X_nameDef} folds the list away and goes, and {FACTION} will hear exactly what was said.
{A_nameDef} looks at the silver for a long time before taking it, then says {DEAD}'s name aloud, once, and that the oath is ended. {X_nameDef} bows low and leaves.
The choice is {A_nameDef}'s, the council says, because the oath was. {A_nameDef} takes a breath at the door and goes out to {X_nameDef}.
{A_nameDef} hears {X_nameDef} out to the end, and then speaks of {DEAD} for a while, as {DEAD} was. When it's done, {A_nameDef} says the oath is laid down.
{X_nameDef} is told that sorry is a word, and {DEAD} was a life. {X_nameDef} doesn't argue, and goes back down the road.
